finding.reasoning: Both frozen rows encode 2.5 G_PER_L, while JCM1023/363 and TOGO1084/357 give 2.5 mL of 8% w/v carbonate stock. This is a liquid-quantity/stage defect, not an instruction to calculate a replacement final dose.

M2649 explicitly measures 10 mL/L of 0.2% w/v ferrous sulfate heptahydrate stock, conflicting with frozen 10 G_PER_L. Current DSMZ503 has a different 0.1% stock specification, so the inventory correctly keeps both the transcription defect and source-version distinction.

M2231 supplies 5 mL of an explicitly defined 6 g/L magnesium sulfate heptahydrate stock. Frozen 5 G_PER_L is not its source quantity. The proposed follow-up correctly retains strength and liquid addition as separate fields.

The original DSMZ1250 formula has calcium nitrate tetrahydrate at 0.02 g; frozen TOGO2531 says pentahydrate. The exact source supports the occurrence-specific four-water correction, not generic five-to-four normalization.

The NIES SOT PDF footnote explicitly replaces 250 mg heptahydrate with 217 mg pentahydrate; M2509 gives the A5stock at 100 mL and a separate 0.1 mL addition. Frozen 217 G_PER_L plus the embedded footnote marker loses both units and hierarchy. The proposed action preserves the source footnote.
